event.prototypReview.title: Prototype review: {project}
event.prototypReview.body: The team suggests replacing “{from}” with “{to}”. It fits the genre better but costs some time. Forecast {before} → {after}.
event.prototypReview.bodyOk: The team is happy with the prototype and has no suggestion.
event.goldReview.title: Gold review: {project}
event.goldReview.body: Production is done. Every further week of testing finds bugs but costs wages. With a day-one patch the press reviews a fixed build (40 % fewer bugs), but the team stays busy for two weeks after release.
event.kritischerBug.title: Critical bug: {project}
event.kritischerBug.body: Shortly before gold, {n} new bugs appear. Delaying costs two weeks and fixes them; a day-one patch lets the press review a fixed build but binds the team after release.
event.auftrag.title: Contract: {kind}
event.auftrag.body: {client} needs help: {weeks} weeks, {pay}, requirement {req} in {area}. Whoever takes it is bound until the deadline. It is fulfilled if q reaches the requirement; otherwise you get 30 % less.
event.bewerbung.title: Application: {name}
event.nachproduktion.title: Sold out: {project}
event.nachproduktion.body: The print run is gone, demand is not. One batch: {units} units for {cost}, available in {weeks} weeks. Expected sales in the following year: about {expected} units, about {revenue}.
event.gate.title: Gate: {project}
event.gate.body: Pre-production or vertical slice is done. Still to invest about {cost}, expected return about {revenue}. What is already spent no longer counts.
event.katalog.messe.title: Trade show
event.katalog.messe.body: The trade show invites exhibitors. A booth makes “{project}” known, but it costs.
event.katalog.interview.title: Interview request
event.katalog.interview.body: A games magazine wants to cover “{project}”. It costs some work time but makes the theme better known.
event.katalog.fortbildung.title: Training for {person}
event.katalog.fortbildung.body: An evening course would improve {person}'s main strength.
event.katalog.entwicklungsrechner.title: Better development machines
event.katalog.entwicklungsrechner.body: A dealer offers faster computers. Bought for everyone, the team gets technically better.
event.katalog.klon.title: A clone of “{product}”
event.katalog.klon.body: Another studio sells a blatant copy. A lawyer could stop it; otherwise your game loses buyers.
event.katalog.radiowerbung.title: Radio ads for “{product}”
event.katalog.radiowerbung.body: A station offers airtime. More buyers, but not for free.
event.katalog.abwerbung.title: {person} has an offer
event.katalog.abwerbung.body: Another studio wants to poach {person}. Keeping them takes a 20 % raise.
event.katalog.jugendschutz.title: Youth protection debate
event.katalog.jugendschutz.body: Newspapers attack “{product}” for its violence. A cut version would calm things down.
event.katalog.betatest.title: Beta test for “{project}”
event.katalog.betatest.body: A computer club offers a beta test: it finds many bugs but costs the team some time.
event.katalog.endspurt.title: Final sprint on “{project}”?
event.katalog.endspurt.body: With overtime the game would be done two weeks earlier. Tired people make more mistakes, though.
event.katalog.hardware1990.title: A new generation of computers
event.katalog.hardware1990.body: The 90s begin: whoever upgrades now develops better technology.
event.katalog.insolvenzwarnung.title: Insolvency warning
event.katalog.insolvenzwarnung.body: The cash is in the red. If it stays there too long, the company is insolvent. The bank wants to know what you will do.
event.katalog.zeitschriftTest.title: Preview for “{project}”
event.katalog.zeitschriftTest.body: A games magazine wants to play an early build of “{project}”. It costs some time but makes the genre better known.
event.katalog.sammlung.title: “{product}” on a compilation
event.katalog.sammlung.body: A mail-order dealer wants “{product}” on a cheap compilation. They pay now, but the compilation takes buyers from the single game.
event.katalog.fanclub.title: A fan club for “{product}”
event.katalog.fanclub.body: Excited players start a fan club and ask for posters and stickers. It costs a little and brings new buyers.
event.katalog.festplatte.title: The hard disk is making noises
event.katalog.festplatte.body: The machine holding the source of “{project}” does not sound healthy. A replacement costs money; if it fails, work is lost.
event.katalog.teamwochenende.title: A weekend for the team
event.katalog.teamwochenende.body: A weekend of games and talks together would make everyone a little better.
event.katalog.gastvortrag.title: {person} is invited to speak
event.katalog.gastvortrag.body: A university invites {person} to talk about making games. Preparing sharpens their own strength, and there is a small fee.
event.katalog.clubTreffen.title: Club night with “{project}”
event.katalog.clubTreffen.body: The local computer club would like to try “{project}”. They find bugs and tell others what they saw.
event.katalog.crash1983.title: The console market collapses
event.katalog.crash1983.body: Too many weak games: retailers are stuck with cartridges, home computers gain.
event.katalog.erholung1986.title: Consoles are back
event.katalog.erholung1986.body: A new manufacturer with strict certification brings the console market back.
event.katalog.pcWende1988.title: The PC takes over
event.katalog.pcWende1988.body: Games for the standard PC become the largest computer market.
event.katalog.cdZeitalter1993.title: The CD era
event.katalog.cdZeitalter1993.body: CD drives spread: CD-quality music and cutscenes become possible.
event.katalog.dreiD1995.title: 3D becomes standard
event.katalog.dreiD1995.body: Polygon graphics take over games; staying 2D looks dated.
event.neubau.title: Engine rebuild recommended
event.neubau.body: Technical debt in the {module} module has reached 80. Updates now cost twice as much. A new major version rebuilds all own modules and sets their debt to 5; it keeps the engine team busy for a while.
event.anforderungVerpasst.title: Missed request: {project}
event.anforderungVerpasst.body: The feature freeze has been reached, but the engine team is not done with “{feature}” ({module} module). Cutting saves the remaining work, postponing waits for the engine, a makeshift solution builds the card at 70% effect and leaves 15 points of debt in the module.
event.markenjubilaeum.title: Brand anniversary: {brand}
event.markenjubilaeum.body: Ten years ago the first title of “{brand}” came out. A collection sells the old games to the fans once more; a remaster brings a game up to date technically.
event.modsKaputt.title: Update breaks mods and saves: {product}
event.modsKaputt.body: After the tech update for “{product}” old saves and fan mods no longer work. The fans are angry.
event.lizenzanfrage.title: License request for your engine
event.lizenzanfrage.body: {studio} wants to license your engine {engine} for its games on the {template} template: {royalty} royalty, flat fee {flat} per game, royalty only above {threshold} revenue per game. Expected income about {perYear} a year. If you accept, your engine is offered commercially; templates and customers are in the engine workshop.
event.grosskunde.title: Major customer asks for your engine
event.grosskunde.body: {studio} wants your engine on the {template} template ({royalty} royalty, flat fee {flat}). Expect about {perYear} a year, a large share of your revenue. The customer negotiates: a royalty discount, source access, or exclusivity in {genre} for a bit more royalty.
event.preisschock.title: Price shock: {engine} raises its royalty
event.preisschock.body: Your engine provider {engine} raises the royalty for existing customers to {royalty}. For your games on this engine that costs about {perYear} more a year.
event.kooperation.title: Cooperation offer
event.kooperation.body: {studio} values working with you and offers its engine {engine} at a friendship price (template {template}): {royalty} royalty, flat fee {flat} per game. If you accept, the contract is ready for your next projects.
quote.perfektionist.hit: {chief} ({studio}): “It is only done when it is good.”
quote.perfektionist.gegenzug: {chief} ({studio}): “We will show how it is done properly.”
quote.showman.hit: {chief} ({studio}): “Did you see the queues outside the shops?”
quote.showman.ziel: {chief} ({studio}): “And this is just the start of the show.”
event.launchAnfrage.title: Launch title wanted
event.launchAnfrage.body: {maker} asks you for a launch title for {platform}. If a game comes out in the first 8 weeks after launch, the maker pays a subsidy of {pay}. You get a devkit right away. Missing the launch costs 10 relationship; declining costs 3.
event.exklusivdeal.title: Exclusive offer for “{project}”
event.exklusivdeal.body: {maker} offers {pay} if “{project}” comes out only on {platform} with no port for a year. Other makers dislike this (relationship −5); {maker} is pleased at release (+10).
event.abwerbung.title: Poaching offer for {person}
event.abwerbung.body: {studio} wants to poach {person}. A counter-offer costs 20 % more salary and adds 15 loyalty; a retention bonus costs 3 months' salary and adds 10. If you let them go, they join {studio}.
event.gehaltsforderung.title: {person} asks for a raise
event.gehaltsforderung.body: After the success of “{project}”, {person} asks for 15 % more salary. Granting it adds 10 loyalty; refusing costs 10.
event.hardwareUpgrade.title: New era: upgrade hardware?
event.hardwareUpgrade.body: Workstations run at only {h} % speed. Upgrading to level {level} costs {cost}.
event.hardwareUpgrade.bodyBroke: Workstations run at only {h} % speed, but there is no money for an upgrade.
event.markenanfrage.title: Request for the brand “{brand}”
event.markenanfrage.body: {studio} wants to license “{brand}” on the {template} template: flat fee {price}, {royalty} royalty, genres {genres}.
event.konkursmasse.title: Bankruptcy auction: “{brand}”
event.konkursmasse.body: {studio} is bankrupt and the brand “{brand}” is up for auction. A bid of {price} wins it; without you it goes to a rival for about {bid}.
event.releaseDuell.title: Competition in your week: {project}
event.releaseDuell.body: {studio} is releasing its title in your release week. Two releases at once split the buyers. Postponing costs interest (10 %, with pre-orders 20 %); more marketing costs 10 % of the development cost so far, once.
event.schutzEntfernen.title: Copy protection cracked: {project}
event.schutzEntfernen.body: The copy protection has been cracked and no longer protects, but still annoys buyers. A patch removes it: players appreciate it, half of the lost satisfaction returns and the studio's reputation rises.
event.rabattwoche.title: Store sale coming up
event.rabattwoche.body: Next week is a store sale. A discount gives a short sales spike, but discounts of 30 % or more teach the brand's fans to wait: future games then sell less at full price. The choice applies to all games on sale.
event.hardwareBundle.title: Hardware bundle: {project}
event.hardwareBundle.body: {maker} wants to bundle {project} with {platform}. Your studio gets a one-off {pay}, and the relationship with {maker} improves.
event.heftBeilage.title: Magazine cover disk: {project}
event.heftBeilage.body: A games magazine wants to put {project} on its cover disk. It pays a one-off {pay}, and the brand becomes better known.
event.verwertung.title: Re-release: {project}
event.verwertung.body.complete: {project} has strong reviews and two expansions. A complete edition at {price} still reaches about {units} buyers. Released within the first year, fans will start waiting for such editions.
event.verwertung.body.budget: {project} hardly sells anymore. A budget re-release at {price} reaches about {units} buyers, using returned stock first. Alternatively a budget publisher pays {fee} plus a 10 % share and takes over pricing.
event.verwertung.body.sammlung: A collection of {n} titles of the brand at {price} reaches about {units} buyers. It tires the brand like half a new title.
event.verwertung.body.klassiker: {project} is ten years old. As a classic on {platform} at {price} it reaches about {units} buyers with a nostalgia bonus.
event.aboDeal.title: Subscription deal: {project}
event.aboDeal.body: A subscription service wants {project} for 12 months and pays {pay} up front. During that time 40 % of full-price sales are lost, but the brand gains fans (5 % of {units} expected buyers).
coach.label: First steps
coach.concept.title: Plan your first game
coach.concept.text: Pick a genre and theme that fit, and features that suit the genre (▲). The bars further down show at once how fit, effort and expected score react. Then start the project.
coach.decision.title: A decision is waiting
coach.decision.text: The decisions panel on the right explains what each option does. If you do not answer, the default applies when the deadline passes.
coach.time.title: Let time run
coach.time.text: Start time at the bottom with 1× (or Space). Your team works week by week; key moments pause the game on their own.
coach.playtest.title: Run a playtest
coach.playtest.text: Under Projects, a playtest shows the expected score and weak spots. Use Steer to swap features while there is still time.
coach.release.title: Your game is done
coach.release.text: Each extra test week finds bugs but costs wages. When the bug curve flattens, open the release package or release with autopilot.
coach.result.title: Learn from the score
coach.result.text: The breakdown shows what carried the score. The knowledge book remembers which combinations worked. Now start your second game and make it better.
event.schwererBug.title: Severe bug found: {product}
event.schwererBug.body: Players of “{product}” report a severe bug. An immediate outsourced hotfix costs {cost}.
event.serverAusfall.title: Launch server outage: {product}
event.serverAusfall.body: At the launch of “{product}” {gap} slots are missing; many cannot get in. A compensation costs {cost}.
event.cheaterWelle.title: Cheater wave: {product}
event.cheaterWelle.body: Cheats are spreading in “{product}”. Better anti-cheat costs {cost}.
event.lootboxDebatte.title: Loot box debate: {product}
event.lootboxDebatte.body: Press and parents criticise the monetization of “{product}”.
event.datenleck.title: Data leak: {product}
event.datenleck.body: Unknown attackers stole account data from “{product}”. Disclosing and compensating costs {cost}.
event.ligaAnfrage.title: A league wants your game: {product}
event.ligaAnfrage.body: A tournament league wants to add “{product}” to its competition. That makes the game better known.
event.merchWahl.title: Merchandise for {brand}
event.merchWahl.body: The brand “{brand}” is well known enough for shirts, figures and mugs. An own fan shop earns double margin but fluctuates and hurts a weak brand; a licence to partners earns a safe share. The choice is permanent.
event.suche.title: Candidates from the search
event.suche.body: The agency presents {n} candidates. Whom do you hire?
event.einstellenVorschlag.title: Suggest shutdown
event.einstellenVorschlag.short: {product}: few players, running at a loss
event.einstellenVorschlag.body: The producers suggest shutting down {product}: the player base is below the threshold and operations cost more than they earn.
event.katalog.crunchEnthuellung.title: A report on your overtime
event.katalog.crunchEnthuellung.body: A trade magazine talked to people on your team: months of crunch. How do you respond?
event.katalog.crunchZweiteWelle.title: Second wave: new crunch accounts
event.katalog.crunchZweiteWelle.body: After your denial more people come forward with proof. The story grows.
event.katalog.leak.title: “{project}” has leaked
event.katalog.leak.body: Screens and details from development are circulating online.
event.katalog.leakZweiteWelle.title: The leak spreads
event.katalog.leakZweiteWelle.body: Unfinished screens shape the game's image; interest drops.
event.katalog.klonUrteil.title: Lawsuit against the clone won
event.katalog.klonUrteil.body: The court rules in your favour: damages, and the clone leaves the shelves.
event.katalog.konsolenEnde.title: Platform discontinued: “{product}”
event.katalog.konsolenEnde.body: The maker no longer builds the device. What happens to your game on it?
event.katalog.verfilmung.title: A film studio wants to adapt “{product}”
event.katalog.verfilmung.body: You get the money now. Whether a film or series helps your brand shows later: having a say costs money but lowers the flop risk; a series sits in between.
event.katalog.filmErfolg.title: The film is a hit
event.katalog.filmErfolg.body: Full cinemas: many people discover your brand.
event.katalog.filmFlop.title: The film flops
event.katalog.filmFlop.body: Panned everywhere; the brand's reputation suffers.
event.katalog.ausfallNachwirkung.title: The outage lingers
event.katalog.ausfallNachwirkung.body: Players who couldn't log in at launch don't come back.
event.katalog.datenleckEntdeckt.title: The hidden data breach comes out
event.katalog.datenleckEntdeckt.body: Journalists found out you kept the breach quiet.
event.katalog.cheaterAbwanderung.title: Players leave over cheaters
event.katalog.cheaterAbwanderung.body: Without countermeasures honest players lose interest.
event.katalog.lootboxBehoerde.title: A regulator examines your loot boxes
event.katalog.lootboxBehoerde.body: After the debate a regulator wants to know if your loot boxes are gambling.
event.katalog.bugShitstorm.title: Backlash over the ignored bug
event.katalog.bugShitstorm.body: Everyone is talking about the severe bug.
event.publisherAbbruch.title: Cancelling a publisher project
event.publisherAbbruch.body: “{project}” is cancelled. By contract you repay the advance received, or the publisher takes over project and brand.
event.katalog.kiWerkzeugWelle.title: AI tools change development
event.katalog.kiWerkzeugWelle.body: New tools write code and build content. Used fully they make you faster, but the team is uneasy and the press is watching.
event.katalog.kiSkandal.title: Scandal over AI content in your games
event.katalog.kiSkandal.body: Players find generated content nobody checked. Your reputation suffers.
event.katalog.letzteKonsolengeneration.b: A maker announces it will only stream from the cloud after this generation and is looking for partners.
event.katalog.letzteKonsolengeneration.o: Become a partner (money and cloud experience)
event.katalog.regulierungswelle.title: New rules for monetisation
event.katalog.regulierungswelle.body: Lawmakers target gambling mechanics and purchase pressure.
event.katalog.regulierungGekippt.title: Court overturns the new rules
event.katalog.regulierungBestaetigt.body: The challenge failed; you have to rebuild anyway.
event.hauptversammlung.title: The shareholders' meeting is unhappy
event.hauptversammlung.body.sparprogramm: Investors demand a savings programme: wage costs −10 % for a year, morale −5. Accepting calms them (+8), refusing angers them (−10).
event.hauptversammlung.body.projektStrei: Investors demand that the newest running project be cancelled. Accepting calms them (+8), refusing angers them (−10).
event.gegenangebot.title: Counteroffer
event.gegenangebot.body: {studio} turns down {bid} but would sell for {counter}.
chain.title: How is a score made?
chain.intro: Every score is a product of a few factors. After each release the breakdown shows how much each factor did.
chain.karten.text: Sum of card values; new cards are worth more, predecessors age.
chain.synergie.text: Matching tags reinforce each other (up to +30 %), some clash.
chain.profil.text: Effort per area against what genre and subgenre expect.
chain.team.text: Strength of the best person per area, plus genre experience.
chain.engine.text: Module levels against the state of the art; cards need levels.
chain.thema.text: Fit of genre and theme; the knowledge book learns it with each release.
chain.bugs.text: Remaining bugs subtract; testing and playtests reduce them.
chain.wertung.text: Quality against press expectations, which rise with the market.
chain.verkauf.text: Score × trend × marketing × platform base × price.
chain.outro: On the design board the score preview shows the first factors before the start; hovering a card shows engine level, effort, tags and synergies.
event.auftrag.bodyTeam: {client} is looking for a team: {n} people for {weeks} weeks, {pay}, requirement {req} in {area} (team average). The team is bound until the deadline and missing from your own projects. It is fulfilled if the average reaches the requirement; otherwise you get 30 % less.
event.katalog.verfilmung.option.serie: License as a series (medium money, later, steadier)
event.katalog.kartellverfahren.title: The competition authority investigates you
event.katalog.kartellverfahren.body: Your market share is too big for the authority. A settlement costs a fifth of your cash; a court case costs three months of budget and can be won or cost two fifths of your cash; conditions lower demand for all your games.
event.katalog.kartellSieg.title: Antitrust case won
event.katalog.kartellSieg.body: The court rules in your favour. The industry is impressed.
event.katalog.kartellNiederlage.title: Antitrust case lost
event.katalog.kartellNiederlage.body: The court imposes a fine of two fifths of your cash.
event.katalog.datenleck.title: Data leak: player data online
event.katalog.datenleck.body: Player data has leaked from your servers. Disclosing costs two months of budget and trust; a cover-up may be exposed and then costs a quarter of your cash and a lot of reputation; hardening costs four months of budget and makes servers pricier.
event.katalog.leckEnthuellt.title: Covered-up data leak exposed
event.katalog.leckEnthuellt.body: The press uncovers the leak. Players leave, the authority imposes a fine of a quarter of your cash.
event.katalog.massenkuendigung.title: A wave of resignations looms
event.katalog.massenkuendigung.body: Morale is low and many have offers from other studios. A raise keeps them, a culture change costs money and rules out crunch, or you let them go.
event.katalog.massenkuendigung.option.ku: Culture change: money, no more crunch
event.katalog.speicherkrise.title: Storage crisis: drives are scarce
event.katalog.speicherkrise.body: Server storage is scarce and expensive. Pay up, clean out old data (annoys players) or buy stock at a high price.
event.katalog.speicherkrise.option.vorra: Buy up stock (three months of budget)
event.katalog.stromkrise.title: Power crisis: data centres under strain
event.katalog.stromkrise.body: Power prices explode. Pay, throttle the servers (players notice) or buy backup power.
event.katalog.stromkrise.option.notstrom: Buy backup power (two months of budget)
